name: Preacher hammer curl
cue: Elbows on the pad; palms facing in, curl up.
research: Seated preacher hammer curl on a cable: a free-standing preacher bench (seat 0.24 H, pad 0.36 H wide sloping 45 deg from vertical on one column between the shins, the cable passing in front of it) with a rope on a low pulley (0.075 H, in a fork on the column's base) in a column 0.6 H (1.1 m) in front of the bench. The body is the machine preacher curl's (research.json biomech.preacher_curl): trunk 10 deg forward, hips about 100, knees 90, feet flat, the backs of the upper arms on the pad (shoulder flexion 55 relative to the trunk, abduction 9), the elbows at the pad's lower end, the elbow from 10 to 120 deg with the upper arm still, but with a neutral grip (palms facing each other, the thumbs up: forearm pronation 90, the wrists within 4 deg of neutral). The pad runs from the armpit to just above the elbow and is placed to meet the back of the arm (fit entry in the patch). Design values from the standard technique description (rope hammer curl on a preacher pad), not a measured trial. A rope end rides in each fist (bone-attached on the hand, so it cannot slip; the grip tunnel stays in the sagittal plane, tilt under 0.2 deg), a knob at the thumb end; two strands of 0.2 H run from the bottom of the fists to a knot that sits on the cable's line, so each strand keeps its length as the knot rides up and forward with the curl (slides kz and ky). The cable leaves the knot 54 deg below horizontal at the bottom, 75 mid-range and 68 deg at the top (the moment arm against the cable, the sine of the angle between the forearm and the cable, is 0.40 at the bottom, 0.99 mid-range and 0.53 at the top). Cable 1:1 to the stack. Geometry: design/cableB/ph.mjs.

targets.note: the research values of the machine preacher curl; the rope and cable are design values (standard technique), not a measured trial

camera.note: The preacher curl view (az 90, el 10), turned 10 deg toward the front and raised 6 deg (az 80, el 16): the near arm shows the brachialis and the brachioradialis as a band along the outer upper arm and the thumb side of the forearm, with the amber biceps in front of them, and the rope and the cable show where the load comes from. Fill 0.62: the seated figure is short, and a larger arm reads better on a phone. The bench stands on a floor rail from the seat post to the pad column and a foot plate under the feet (a plate under everything would run under the exercise name on the phone); the column crops at the top.
